items.title: Topic Fourteen, Sub-Part 5: Seeing Another's Wrongdoing, and Reading the Fruit of Karma Rightly (continued)

items.zh: 即彼又見種種有情身相差別。或有生盲、生聾、生瘂、或瞎、或跛、或癬、或癩、或復短壽、或惡形色、或多疾病、或貧賤家、或少支屬、或弊惡慧、或扇宅迦、或半宅迦、或醜形類，餘即不爾。見已便作如是思惟：觀觀是人，先作種種惡不善業，今受如是苦惡果報；乃至止止如是惡不善業，餘如前說。即彼又見他人黠慧，無有嬾惰，具足翹勇。所謂能作營農、商賈、行船等業，及能正作言論事業。彼雖具足如是翹勇，所作事業數漸衰損，終無成辦。見已便作如是思惟，餘如前說。即彼又見二人出家，趣於非家，同修梵行。一、於衣服、飲食等利有所匱乏，一則不爾。見已便作如是思惟，餘如前說。即彼又見或有國王，或是王等，大地封疆咸皆克伏，堅著不捨。但為一身一具骸骨，唯為現在少小安樂，身語意門現行無量廣大惡行，損壞多生多身安樂，當受多生多身大苦。見已便作如是思惟：觀觀是王、或是王等甚為愚弊，唯知保愛一生一身，不知保愛多生多身，唯愛現在少時小樂，不愛當來多時大樂，亦非不愛多生重苦；乃至止止如是惡不善業，終不應為、終不應作、終不應行、終不應犯。復有或善男子、或善女人，為性聰慧，獲得天眼；用此天眼見諸有情死時、生時，如經廣說，乃至生在大那落迦中。見已便作如是思惟：觀觀是人、於現法中造作如是惡不善業，令受後法辛楚果報；乃至止止如是惡不善業。餘如前說。如是或善男子、或善女人，見他所作諸惡業已，由四種行，諦善思惟、諦善觀察。何等為四？一者、觀察或因違越，或邪活命，或放逸懈怠，於現法中造作種種惡不善業，即現法受非愛果報。二者、觀察或有有情依身差別，或有所作而不果遂，或有所求而不果遂，皆由先造惡不善業，故現法中各受如是非愛果報。三者、觀察或有國王或與王等，因現法中行諸惡業，比知當來定受種種非愛果報。四者、觀察諸有情類死時、生時，因現法中造作種種惡不善業，後法中受非愛果報。彼由如是如實知故，終不自作。云何業縛？謂樂諸業故，由業重故，於業果報不自在故。樂諸業者，謂如有一，串習惡故，愛樂諸惡。由此因緣，於諸善法心不能入。是初業縛。由業重者，謂如有一，於無間業，或有具造，或不具造。由此因緣，雖有欣樂於佛所證善說正法毘柰耶中，暫時出家尚不能得，況當能獲沙門果證。如是名為第二業縛。於業果報不自在者，謂如有一，由身語意惡行因緣，生諸惡趣。生彼處已，不得自在，不能自任長夜受苦；或生邊地，於彼絕無四賢善眾，所謂苾芻，廣說乃至鄔波斯迦。如是名為第三業縛。復次，今當略辨上所說義。謂薄伽梵於此略示，依諸有情業業果報，如理思惟；及顯如理思惟為先，法隨法行。當知是名此中略義。
items.en: They also see the differences in the bodies of various beings: some born blind, born deaf, born mute; some one-eyed, lame, scabby, or leprous; some short-lived, of ugly appearance, or much afflicted by illness; some of poor and low family, with few relatives, or of bad understanding; some ṣaṇḍhakas or paṇḍakas, or of ugly form; while others are not so. Seeing this, they reflect: 'Look, look at these people: earlier they did all kinds of evil, unwholesome deeds, and now they receive such painful, bad results.' And so on up to: 'Stop, stop! Such evil, unwholesome deeds…', the rest as before. They also see others who are clever, not lazy, and full of energy, able to farm, trade, sail ships, and so on, and able to carry on the work of discussion properly. Yet although they have such energy, what they undertake gradually declines again and again and is never accomplished. Seeing this, they reflect in this way; the rest is as before. They also see two people who have gone forth from home into homelessness and practise the holy life together; one lacks gain in robes, food, and the like, and the other does not. Seeing this, they reflect in this way; the rest is as before. They also see a king, or one equal to a king, who has subdued all the lands of the great earth and clings to them firmly without letting go; for the sake of one body, one set of bones, for a little happiness in the present, through the doors of body, speech, and mind, he commits countless great evil deeds, destroys the happiness of many lives and many bodies, and will undergo great suffering in many lives and many bodies. Seeing this, they reflect: 'Look, look at this king, or this one equal to a king: how foolish and wretched he is! He knows only how to cherish one life and one body, and does not know how to cherish many lives and many bodies; he loves only a little happiness for a short time in the present and does not love great happiness for a long time in the future, nor does he shrink from heavy suffering in many lives.' And so on up to: 'Stop, stop! Such evil, unwholesome deeds should never be done, never be made, never be practised, never be committed.' Further, a son or daughter of good family, intelligent by nature, who has gained the divine eye, sees with this divine eye beings dying and being born, as explained at length in the sūtra, up to being born in the great hells. Seeing this, they reflect: 'Look, look at this person: in this present life they did such evil, unwholesome deeds and so receive bitter results in a later life.' And so on up to: 'Stop, stop! Such evil, unwholesome deeds…', the rest as before. In this way, a son or daughter of good family, having seen the evil deeds done by others, reflects carefully and examines carefully in four ways. What are the four? First, they observe that through transgression, wrong livelihood, or heedlessness and laziness, people do various evil, unwholesome deeds in this present life and receive unwanted results in this present life. Second, they observe that differences in beings' bodies, undertakings that are not accomplished, and seeking that is not fulfilled are all due to evil, unwholesome deeds done before, and so each receives such unwanted results in this present life. Third, they observe that a king, or one equal to a king, through the evil deeds he does in this present life, will certainly receive various unwanted results in the future, as one infers. Fourth, they observe beings dying and being born, and that through the various evil, unwholesome deeds done in this present life they receive unwanted results in a later life. Because they know this as it really is, they never do such deeds themselves. What is the bondage of karma? It is delighting in karma, the weight of karma, and lack of mastery over the results of karma. Delighting in karma: someone, through habituation to evil, loves and delights in evil; for this reason their mind cannot enter into wholesome dharmas. This is the first bondage of karma. The weight of karma: someone has committed the uninterrupted deeds, in full or in part; for this reason, although they may delight in the well-taught true Dharma and Vinaya realised by the Buddha, they cannot go forth even for a while, let alone attain the fruits of the ascetic life. This is called the second bondage of karma. Lack of mastery over the results of karma: someone, because of bad conduct of body, speech, and mind, is born in bad destinies. Once born there, they have no mastery and cannot help themselves, suffering through the long night; or they are born in a border land where there are none of the four good assemblies, namely monks, and so on at length up to laywomen. This is called the third bondage of karma. Further, the meaning of what was said above will now be briefly set out. Here the Blessed One briefly shows reflecting appropriately on beings' karma and the results of karma, and shows that, with appropriate reflection first, one practises the Dharma in accordance with the Dharma. It should be understood that this is the summary meaning here.

blocks.text: The last day of fascicle 18. **All of today's Chinese is missing from Ru-Yi's translation**; the English column gives our own translation, and the commentary summarises it.

The wise person goes on reflecting on what they see: - **Differences among beings:** some born blind, deaf, or mute; lame; diseased; short-lived; ugly; poor; with few relatives; dull; and others not. "Look: this person did evil before and now receives this result. Stop!" - **Effort that fails:** someone clever and energetic in farming, trade, or shipping whose work keeps failing. - **Two monks:** two who went forth together; one lacks robes and food, the other does not. - **Kings:** a king who conquers lands and clings to them, and for one body, one skeleton, a little pleasure in this life, commits vast wrongs that will cost him many lives of suffering. "How foolish: he loves one life and not many lives; a little pleasure now and not great happiness later." - **The divine eye:** one with the divine eye sees beings die and be reborn, even in the great hells, according to their deeds.

**Four ways of reflecting:** on wrongs that bring results in this life; on present differences that come from past wrongs; on present wrongs from which future results can be inferred (the king); and on deaths and rebirths seen directly. Knowing this, one never does such things oneself.

**Three bonds of karma:** 1. **Delight in actions:** habituated to evil, one delights in it and cannot enter the good. 2. **Heavy actions:** one who has committed one of the five heinous deeds cannot even go forth, still less attain the fruits. 3. **No freedom from results:** born in a bad destiny, or in a border land without monks, nuns, or lay followers, one has no chance to practise.

In brief: reflect rightly on beings' actions and their results, and let right reflection lead to practise in accord with the Dharma. Master Cháng Bǎi: dwelling on others' faults with anger is the opposite of this; the purpose is to learn, not to condemn.
The essential-body verses have touched every part of life: renown and wealth, fear, solitude, craving, heedfulness, karma. Fascicle 19 completes the Stage of Reflection.

quiz.q: "Action itself binds" — what is the first way, per Master Cháng Bǎi, that action becomes a bond?
options: habituation — habits form by repeated practice, and doing something again and again becomes a bond
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: habits are cultivated — formed by repetition, practising again and again, doing it ceaselessly, until it becomes a bond. Venerable Miào Jìng: if great greed or anger arises, meditation is affected and the mind cannot enter wholesome states.

quiz.q: At the fascicle's close, what does Master Cháng Bǎi warn against when seeing another's wrongdoing, and why?
options: not to dwell on others' faults — doing so accords with anger and leads to wanting to harm them by body, speech, and mind
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: when one dwells on another's faults, one is in fact accompanied by anger; accompanied by anger, one wants to commit evil deeds of body, speech, and mind to destroy the other.
